evidence.heading: N2 instructions — Section B: When to use a different notice
evidence.text:
SECTION
B When to use a different notice

There are three other notices that a landlord can use when increasing a tenant’s rent:

• Use Form N1 to increase the rent for any rental unit (other than a care home
rental unit) that is covered by the rules limiting rent increases under the RTA.
• Use Form N3 (Notice to Increase the Rent and/or Charges for Care Services and
Meals) to increase the rent for any care home unit that is covered by the rules
limiting rent increases under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006.
• Use Form N10 if you and the tenant have agreed to increase the rent above the
guideline because you:
 have done or will do capital work, or
 have provided or will provide a new or additional service.

required_claims.text: For an ordinary increase under the RTA rules limiting rent increases, the N1 mapping for covered rental units excludes care-home rental units.

statements.text: For an ordinary increase, Form N1 is used for any rental unit covered by the RTA rules limiting rent increases.

c1.coverage_basis: The required claim excludes covered care-home units from N1, but the answer includes any covered rental unit; the source specifies N3 for that excluded category.

citation_basis.summary: The own passage limits N1 to non-care-home units and cannot support the universal claim.

factual_basis.summary: The source specifies N3 for covered care-home units, a counterexample to N1 for any covered rental unit.
